text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - node.gpu-046 kernel-panic detected; kubelet NotReady. Pager: platform-oncall -> oncall rotation. Host: gpu-046 (10.4.12.46). Incident ID: PD-89421.

alex: acked. I’m on it.

sasha: I saw latency spike on serving-cluster-1 ~10s ago, routing fallback kicked in for some requests. Not seeing 5xx spike yet but token-level latency moved up.

miguel: noted. Are we seeing OOMs on pods or full node crash?

alex: Node is reporting kernel OOPS + reboot loop. Kubelet flapping. SSH to host times out intermittently. Boot logs (from last successful journal pull):
```
Kernel panic - not syncing: fatal exception
CPU: 1 PID: 1234 Comm: kubelet Not tainted
Call Trace:
  dump_stack+0x6d/0x8b
  panic+0x12a/0x1f0
  ? gpu_driver_fault+0x100/0x200
```

alex: Looks like a GPU driver crash followed by kernel panic.

anya: Customer impact check: which customers have active traffic on gpu-046?

alex: Pulling from scheduler: model-serving pods on that node: redwood-gen-1 (2 pods), reranker-v2 (1 pod). Autoscaler moved some replicas earlier today but those remaining are pinned by nodeAffinity.

sasha: Quick mitigation: cordon -> drain non-critical pods, rely on smart routing to move traffic. If kubelet is down we may not be able to evict gracefully.

miguel: Run commands to cordon and try to evict:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-046
kubectl drain gpu-046 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

alex: Trying cordon now.

incident-bot: Action logged: alex cordoned node gpu-046.

alex: Cordon succeeded. Drain is timing out on some pods (kubelet not responding). For the pinned pods I'll create replacements on other nodes and update routing.

sasha: Start manual replica increase for redwood-gen-1 in cluster region-us-east:
```
kubectl scale deploy/redwood-gen-1 --replicas=4 -n production
```

anya: Messaging: customer-impact: low-medium. A few requests routed to fallback model variant (slower) for customers on reserved capacity. No major 5xx so far. I'll prep a status note but hold until we know containment. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

miguel: If host won't rejoin, propose retire node and schedule maintenance. Escalating to infra team for hardware triage. @platform-oncall can you pick up if reboot fails?

platform-oncall: I’m available. If node keeps kernel panicking we should power-cycle via IPMI and then collect full dmesg and nvdec logs, and open a maintenance ticket with cloud provider.

alex: IPMI timed out earlier but will try a remote power-cycle now.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Escalation to SRE after 6 minutes with no kubelet recovery.

alex: power-cycle initiated via BMC. Waiting for console.

(small wait)

alex: Host rebooted but hits fsck prompt on root. Might be disk corruption from panic. Kernel still shows nvdec errors in early boot.

platform-oncall: Plan B: mark node as unschedulable permanently, remove from active pool. Run `kubectl delete node gpu-046` after confirming pods are rescheduled. Record in inventory.

anya: Customer comms: sending brief note to customers on affected reservations: "We've detected an infrastructure issue impacting a subset of GPU hosts in us-east. Traffic is being routed to alternate capacity and fallback models; you may see modest latency increases. We're actively remediating and will update in 30 minutes."

miguel: Logging runbook steps I followed in the thread:
- attempted graceful drain (blocked by kubelet)
- cordon succeeded
- scaled replicas to move load off node
- initiated BMC power-cycle
- flagged node for hardware ticket if fails further

alex: After power-cycle, node booted but kernel panicked again within ~5 minutes. Repeating the cycle does not look promising. I recommend retiring node now.

platform-oncall: Agreed. I'll take node out and start maintenance workflow: open provider ticket, attach kernel panic logs, collect physical serial console dump, and schedule on-call hardware engineer tomorrow morning for RMA if needed.

sasha: From app side, I’m enabling stricter fallback routes for model-serving to avoid trying to schedule on drained/retiring nodes. Also adding a temporary rule in routing: prefer dedicated pools with >= 2 healthy nodes.

anya: Current assessment for incident summary: impact=partial, scope=single-rack (4 hosts noticed elevated errors), customer-visible latency bump and some slow fallbacks, no widespread 5xx. Action: retire gpu-046, open hardware ticket, monitor related hosts for driver regressions, escalate to infra for driver/kernel regression test.

incident-bot: Incident update recorded. Incident state: mitigation in progress -> containment. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.

alex: Handing off to platform-oncall for hardware/maintenance follow-up. I’ll update runbook with logs I saved to /var/logs/incidents/PD-89421.tar.gz and leave traces in the console ticket.

platform-oncall: Taking over. If anything changes ping me directly @platform-oncall. :white_check_mark:

anya: Thanks team. I'll draft a short post-incident note once we confirm root cause (driver vs hardware).

sasha: :thumbsup: Good triage.

miguel: Closing loop: created maintenance ticket MT-22319 with provider and attached kernel dumps and serial console.

platform-oncall: Logged. Setting node state to retired in inventory. Will follow up on RMA and kernel driver trace.

alex: marking thread as handoff complete.

incident-bot: Thread closed for on-call rotation (handoff recorded)
